claim.pdf_says: A.4.3   Commit and Rollback  (printed as a third-level sub-clause of A.4, in the same bold heading style as 'A.4.1   General' and 'A.4.2   ACCEPT and DISPLAY screen handling' on page 974)
claim.why_it_matters: A.4.1 and A.4.2 are transcribed as '### A.4.1 General' / '### A.4.2 ACCEPT and DISPLAY screen handling' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 39849 and 39864), but A.4.3 is emitted at '##', the same level as its own parent '## A.4 Optional language element list' (line 39846). That makes the Commit-and-Rollback optional-element list a sibling of A.4 instead of a child, so any tool or reader navigating by heading depth loses the containment relation and A.4's item list appears to end at A.4.2. The same demotion affects A.4.4 through A.4.11 (lines 39948-40035) while A.4.12-A.4.14 (lines 40103-40115) are correctly at '###', so the file is internally inconsistent about the depth of one and the same clause level.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. Every raw observation in the claim is factually accurate, but the finding is a markdown-styling inconsistency, not a discrepancy between the PDF and its transcription. Four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The kind is 'missing-heading', but the heading is present verbatim. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 39928-39929 reads '' / '## A.4.3 Commit and Rollback'. The rendered page (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1005/spec_p1005.png, printed page 975, bottom of body text above the '(c)ISO/IEC 2023 975' footer) prints 'A.4.3 Commit and Rollback'. Text, clause number, capitalisation and word order match character-for-character. The clause's own five-item list is likewise complete on the following page (lines 39937-39945: Commit and Rollback 9.1.18; IO-CONTROL APPLY COMMIT 12.4.6.3; EC-FLOW-APPLY-COMMIT/EC-FLOW-COMMIT/EC-FLOW-ROLLBACK; COMMIT statement 14.9.7; ROLLBACK statement 14.9.36). No normative content is lost, altered, reordered, or made ambiguous. (2) THE PDF CARRIES NO PRINTED DEPTH SIGNAL TO LOSE. I cropped and magnified the printed glyphs. 'A.4 Optional language element list' and 'A.4.1 General' (page 974, crops crop_a4_a41.png) and 'A.4.3 Commit and Rollback' (page 975, crop crop_a43b.png) are set in the IDENTICAL bold serif face, at the identical point size, with the identical 'numberTitle' layout and identical left margin. ISO does not typographically distinguish the second-level clause A.4 from the third-level clauses A.4.1/A.4.2/A.4.3 at all. The claim's premise that A.4.3 is 'printed as a third-level sub-clause ... in the same bold heading style as A.4.1 and A.4.2' is true only in the trivial sense that A.4 is in that same style too. The sole depth indicator printed anywhere is the dotted clause number itself -- and the transcription preserves that number verbatim inside the heading text. So the '##' vs '###' choice is not a transcription of anything on the page; it is an editorial markdown-styling decision downstream of the source, and no reader or tool keyed on the clause number can be misled. (3) THE STATED HARM DOES NOT DEPEND ON THIS HEADING. The claim argues a depth-navigating consumer 'loses the containment relation' and 'A.4's item list appears to end at A.4.2'. That breakage is already unconditional in this file, independent of A.4.3's level: page-break furniture is emitted as '##' headings throughout, and it lands INSIDE the very clauses at issue -- '## Page 1004' (line 39831) immediately precedes '## A.4', '## Page 1005' (line 39878) sits between A.4.2's item 4 and item 5, and '## Page 1006' (line 39933) sits between the A.4.3 heading and A.4.3's own item list. A tool navigating by heading depth therefore already sees 'Page 1005' and 'Page 1006' as siblings of A.4 and as interlopers splitting every clause body. Heading depth is not, and by this file's page-marker convention cannot be, a containment carrier anywhere in the transcription. Promoting A.4.3 to '###' would not restore containment for A.4.2 or A.4.3; the page markers still sever both. (4) IT IS FORMATTING, AND IT CHANGES NO MEANING. The rejection criteria explicitly exclude differences that are page-break furniture or formatting, and differences that do not change meaning. Markdown '#'-count is presentation. No COBOL syntax, general rule, syntax rule, format diagram, choice indicator, cross-reference, or clause number is affected. The list of optional Commit-and-Rollback language elements a conformance implementer must support is byte-identical to the standard either way. For the record, the sub-observation that the file is internally inconsistent IS verifiable and I confirmed it: grep of '^#{1,6} *A\.4' gives A.4 at '##' (39846), A.4.1/A.4.2 at '###' (39849, 39864), A.4.3 through A.4.11 at '##' (39929, 39948, 39957, 39962, 39967, 39990, 39997, 40026, 40035), and A.4.12/A.4.13/A.4.14 back at '###' (40103, 40108, 40115). That is a real cosmetic wart in the markdown and a fine janitorial cleanup, but it is a defect of the transcription's own house style rather than an infidelity to the ISO PDF, which is what this ledger adjudicates. Logged as not-real; no spec-reconciliation action warranted.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy. The heading 'A.4.3 Commit and Rollback' is transcribed verbatim and completely (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 39929), together with its full five-item optional-element list. The only difference is the markdown heading level: A.4.3-A.4.11 are emitted at '##' while their siblings A.4.1, A.4.2 and A.4.12-A.4.14 are at '###'. The ISO PDF prints A.4, A.4.1, A.4.2 and A.4.3 in one and the same bold face, size and layout, so there is no printed depth distinction being transcribed incorrectly -- the hierarchy is conveyed solely by the dotted clause number, which the markdown preserves. The claimed navigational harm is moot besides, since '## Page NNNN' break markers are emitted at '##' inside these same clauses and already prevent heading depth from expressing containment anywhere in the file. Residual value: an optional cosmetic normalisation of the A.4.x heading levels for internal consistency, carrying no conformance or content impact.
